neighbours.label: a conventional system for reading time, numbers or writing: the clock's hour or minute hand, Arabic or Roman numerals, a calendar, a script
fire: At noon the hour hand of the tower clock covers the other one.
The dial on this old watch is marked with Roman numerals.
The shop sign was written in Cyrillic script and hard to read.
Their festivals follow the Hebrew calendar rather than the Gregorian calendar.
The second hand of my kitchen clock has stopped moving.
Page numbers in the preface appear in small Roman numerals.
The name of the town is spelled in Devanagari script on the map.
The farmers still count their months by the old lunar calendar.
quiet: At noon the old bell of the tower rings over the square.
The strap on this old watch is made of soft brown leather.
The shop sign was painted bright blue and hard to miss.
Their festivals take place in the village rather than in the city.
The left hand of my kitchen helper has a small burn.
Page corners in the preface appear yellow and slightly torn.
The name of the town is printed in large letters on the map.
The farmers still sell their grain at the old town market.

notes: Card: ' hand' x3 (clock), ' numer' x3, ' script' x2, ' calendar', 'Gregorian Months', ' abbreviated', '位' (unit). Probe: 'minute hand' 0.667; 'Arabic numerals' 0.633; 'Arabic script' 0.563; 'its own calendar' 0.167; 'held his hand' 0.010; 'Arabic class' 0.032. The shared pattern is a convention for reading a value; new cases in the test are Roman numerals, Cyrillic, Hebrew and hour hands.
